cards.title: IVIVE Error Sources and Low-Clearance Challenges
cards.claim: Systematic underprediction in IVIVE is multifactorial, stemming from enzyme activity loss, cofactor depletion, measurement errors in fraction unbound, and unstirred water layer effects. Low clearance compounds are difficult to measure accurately due to low turnover rates, leading to high uncertainty in first-dose estimations. Interlaboratory variability in hepatocyte intrinsic clearance values is significant and not dependent on the number of prediction values.
conditions: Consider when evaluating the reliability of IVIVE-derived clearance predictions.
Note that compounds with lower rotatable bonds and lower lipophilicity may show different variability patterns.
Uniform in vitro values do not guarantee accurate predictions; many uniform predictions are inaccurate.
required_inputs: Source of in vitro data (single vs. multi-lab).
Physicochemical properties (logD, rotatable bonds) if available for context.
Intrinsic clearance values and their variability metrics.
limitations: Experimental procedures (e.g., shaking during incubation) affect results.
Low turnover compounds have large uncertainty in clearance estimation.
High intrinsic clearance compounds also show increased error due to cofactor depletion/permeability limits.
cards.downstream_use: Qualifies the confidence level of IVIVE-based human clearance predictions.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
